snarer.title: The Snarer
snarer.idea: IT HAS ALREADY SET THE ROOM - it drives you onto its own lines
snarer.feed_line: The lines were here before you.

drillmaster.title: The Drillmaster
drillmaster.idea: IT SUMMONS - it beats the muster and the garrison forms up

scrapwright.title: The Scrapwright
scrapwright.idea: IT ARMOURS ITSELF - every plate knocked off is replaced from the floor

gaoler.title: Shacklemaw
gaoler.idea: IT DRAGS - the hook takes one out of the line and reels them in
gaoler.feed_line: A chain is paying out in the dark.

snuffer.title: The Snuffer
snuffer.idea: IT TAKES THE LIGHT - it puts out the lamps one at a time
snuffer.feed_line: The nearest lamp has gone out.

sexton.title: The Sexton
sexton.idea: IT WILL NOT STAY DOWN - it carries its own graves; empty the lit niches
sexton.feed_line: A spade is working somewhere in the dark.

porter.title: The Porter
porter.idea: IT BARS THE WAY - it drops a leaf across the door: no retreat, no help
porter.feed_line: A bar has dropped behind you.

tallyman.title: The Tallyman
tallyman.idea: IT TAKES AND LEAVES - it lifts your gear, wears it and withdraws
tallyman.feed_line: Something is counting what you carry.

cook.title: The Cook
cook.idea: IT KEEPS THE PACK ALIVE - the pot heals the room; spill the pot

sluicekeeper.title: The Sluicekeeper
sluicekeeper.idea: IT RAISES THE WATER - it winds the sluice open a step at a time

sower.title: The Sower
sower.idea: IT PLANTS THE GROUND AGAINST YOU - what it casts stands up as thorn

stoker.title: The Stoker
stoker.idea: IT IS ONLY AS BIG AS THE FIRE - starve the pit and it starves

bellman.title: The Bellman
bellman.idea: IT RINGS FROM WHERE IT IS NOT - the sound comes from the wrong place
bellman.feed_line: A bell, and not where you thought.

boiler.title: Scaldmere
boiler.idea: IT POURS AND IT SETS - the floor hardens around your feet

tallyman_chibi.title: The Tallyman (chibi)
tallyman_chibi.idea: IT TAKES AND LEAVES - rebuilt in the game's own register
tallyman_chibi.feed_line: Something is counting what you carry.

cook_chibi.title: The Cook (chibi)
cook_chibi.idea: IT KEEPS THE PACK ALIVE - rebuilt in the game's own register

sluicekeeper_chibi.title: The Sluicekeeper (chibi)
sluicekeeper_chibi.idea: IT RAISES THE WATER - rebuilt in the game's own register

sower_chibi.title: The Sower (chibi)
sower_chibi.idea: IT PLANTS THE GROUND AGAINST YOU - rebuilt in the game's own register

boiler_chibi.title: The Boiler (chibi)
boiler_chibi.idea: IT POURS AND IT SETS - rebuilt in the game's own register

snarer_chibi.title: The Snarer (chibi)
snarer_chibi.idea: IT HAS ALREADY SET THE ROOM - rebuilt in the game's own register
snarer_chibi.feed_line: The lines were here before you.

gaoler_chibi.title: Shacklemaw (chibi)
gaoler_chibi.idea: IT DRAGS - rebuilt in the game's own proportions
gaoler_chibi.feed_line: A chain is paying out in the dark.

porter_chibi.title: The Porter (chibi)
porter_chibi.idea: IT BARS THE WAY - rebuilt in the game's own register
porter_chibi.feed_line: A bar has dropped behind you.

sexton_chibi.title: The Sexton (chibi)
sexton_chibi.idea: IT WILL NOT STAY DOWN - rebuilt in the game's own register
sexton_chibi.feed_line: A spade is working somewhere in the dark.

stoker_chibi.title: The Stoker (chibi)
stoker_chibi.idea: IT IS ONLY AS BIG AS THE FIRE - rebuilt in the game's own proportions

snuffer_chibi.title: The Snuffer (chibi)
snuffer_chibi.idea: IT TAKES THE LIGHT - rebuilt in the game's own register
snuffer_chibi.feed_line: The nearest lamp has gone out.

jointer.title: The Jointer
jointer.idea: IT COMES APART AND BOTH HALVES KEEP WORKING - drive the pin or break it and there are two

quartermaster.title: The Quartermaster
quartermaster.idea: IT ARMS THE ROOM - everything else in here takes a weapon off its sheaf

loader.title: The Loader
loader.idea: IT WEIGHS YOU DOWN - it loads you, and you fight slower until you drop it
loader.feed_line: Something is putting a load on you.

hurdleman.title: The Hurdleman
hurdleman.idea: IT CUTS THE ROOM IN TWO - it plants a hurdle through your line and you fight it two and two
hurdleman.feed_line: A hurdle just went down between you.

tanner.title: The Tanner
tanner.idea: IT WILL NOT TAKE THE SAME BLOW TWICE - what hurts it once it pegs a fresh hide over; change your answer or stop hurting it
tanner.feed_line: It is pegging up a fresh hide.

reeve.title: The Reeve
reeve.idea: IT TAKES THE HAUL - while it stands the floor pays its box and not you; break the box or walk out of here with nothing
reeve.feed_line: It is here for the lord's share.

tapster.title: The Tapster
tapster.idea: IT DRINKS WHAT YOU BROUGHT - every brew raised in this room goes into its tun and not into the hero; run it dry or your line breaks and walks out

pressman.title: The Pressman
pressman.idea: IT PRESSES YOUR FALLEN - a hero that goes down in this room is collared and stood back up on ITS side; get them up, or break the yoke, before the collar shuts
pressman.feed_line: Irons just came off the yoke.

strickler.title: The Strickler
strickler.idea: IT STRIKES YOU LEVEL - while it stands, your best hero is scraped down to the measure of your worst; your strongest is no answer, so lift the lowest or break the beam
strickler.feed_line: Something in here is taking the heap off.

dyer.title: The Dyer
dyer.idea: IT MARKS ONE OF YOU AND HUNTS ONLY THE MARK - it slings the vat, and while the stain is wet it will walk past everyone else to reach the one wearing it; the stain can be passed hero to hero, so the party chooses who carries it and for how long
dyer.feed_line: Something back there just marked one of you.

greener.title: The Greener
greener.idea: IT GREENS YOUR IRON - every blow landed on it leaves the weapon a little more eaten, and a bitten weapon bites less; a hero can stop and scrape it clean, which costs them the time they would have spent swinging, so the party is not choosing how to kill it but how long each of them can afford to keep hitting it

moulder.title: The Moulder
moulder.idea: IT TAKES YOUR SHAPE - it presses one of your heroes into its sand bed and pours, and what stands up out of the box fights with that hero's reach and that hero's swing; the party is not choosing how to kill it but which of them it is allowed to read, so the hero who leads is the hero they will have to fight, and the mould can be broken before the metal sets
moulder.feed_line: It took a copy of one of you.

ratcatcher.title: Skivven
ratcatcher.idea: IT IS PAID BY THE TAIL - everything else that dies in this room goes into the cage on its hip and it is stronger for every bay it fills, so the party is not choosing how to kill it but whether to clear the room at all; leave the lesser things standing and you fight the whole floor at once, clear them and you hand this one the fight, and the bays already filled can be cut open to give them back
ratcatcher.feed_line: It is paid by the tail.

drover.title: The Drover
drover.idea: IT YOKES ONE OF YOU - it closes a bow of its own yoke on a hero and after that the harm you do it travels the chain: while the collar holds, every blow landed on the Drover is paid half by the one wearing it, so the party is not choosing how hard to hit but whether to hit at all; cut the chain and the yoke comes free to take the next, and the second bow hangs open to tell you it can

paviser.title: Shieldmaw
paviser.idea: IT KEEPS ITS FACE TO YOU - it carries a pavise on a hinge post and swings it onto whoever is hurting it most, and a blow into the board does nothing at all; so the party cannot win this by standing still and hitting harder - one of you has to get round the post while another holds its attention, and the moment you two swap sides the board swings back
paviser.feed_line: A board came round to face you.

fenman.title: The Fenman
fenman.idea: IT TAKES WHAT STIRS - it is hooded blind and it hunts by disturbance, so it comes for whoever moved last: swing, step, drink, and you are the one it wants. A hero who stands perfectly still is not there as far as it is concerned - and a hero who stands perfectly still is also doing nothing. So the party cannot all fight and cannot all hide; somebody has to stir, and the fight is the argument about who and when

comfitmaker.title: The Comfitmaker
comfitmaker.idea: IT GIVES YOU THE ONLY THING THAT CUTS IT - its shell is sugar-hard and nothing the party carries marks it, but it hands out comfits as it fights and a comfit is the one thing that does. Take one and you can hurt it; the sugar also gums the hand that took it, so that hero swings slower for as long as they hold it. The party cannot hurt it without accepting something from it, and the stand says how many are left
comfitmaker.feed_line: Everything in here is sweet and none of it is kind.

leech.title: The Leech
leech.idea: IT WILL NOT LET A WOUND CLOSE - while it stands nothing in this room mends. Every point of healing the party spends is drawn off into the basin at its side, and the Leech spends what the basin holds on itself, so the level in that basin is the mending you paid for. Tip the basin and it has nothing to mend with and your own healing comes back; leave it standing and your healer is carrying water in a sieve
leech.feed_line: It will have the bad blood out of you, and keep it.

beadle.title: The Beadle
beadle.idea: IT CALLS THE ORDER - while it stands the party does not choose who acts. The Beadle calls, and it calls the same hero again and again while the rest hold their ground and watch; the four brass pegs on the board it holds overhead are the calls it has left and you can count them from the door. Knock the board off its arm and the order comes back to you
beadle.feed_line: It says who speaks, and it is not you.

rammer.title: The Rammer
rammer.idea: IT DROPS ON THE COUNT - it hauls the monkey to the head of the frame, it holds, and it lets go. Whatever is standing on the pile when the monkey falls is finished, and you can HEAR it coming: the haul is slow and the hold is the warning. The answer is not what you do, it is when - stand off the pile for the drop and come back in while it hauls
rammer.feed_line: Something is being driven into the floor.

fuller.title: The Fuller
fuller.idea: IT GIVES BACK WHAT YOU PUT IN - every blow you land soaks into the cloth in its trough, and when the cloth is full it wrings the lot out over the room at once. The cloth is the gauge and you can see it swell, so the fight is a decision nothing else in here asks for: STOP HITTING IT. Break the stocks, or wring it early and eat a small one, or keep swinging and pay for every blow you landed
fuller.feed_line: Something in here is taking the blows.

stackman.title: The Stackman
stackman.idea: IT GETS ABOVE YOUR REACH - every time you hurt it it pitches a fresh sheaf under its own feet and climbs a course, and from up there nothing with a hand on it can touch it; it pitches down at you for free. The stack is the gauge and you can count the courses from the doorway, so this is the one fight in here that asks about your PARTY and not your footing: cut the bottom course out from under it, or bring something with reach, or watch it climb out of the fight entirely
stackman.feed_line: Something up there is building itself higher.

dauber.title: Wetwall
dauber.idea: IT WALLS YOU IN - every time you hurt it it lays a fresh course across the room and the floor you have left to fight on gets smaller. The course goes up WET, and while it is wet it can be broken by anything; once it sets, nothing the party carries will open it again. So the fight is a choice that expires: swing at the Dauber, or spend the same swing on the wall it just laid, and the hod on its shoulder says how many courses it still has to give you
dauber.feed_line: Something is laying up a wall behind you.

sealer.title: Leadbite
sealer.idea: IT SEALS WHAT YOU CARRY - every bite of the press shuts ONE hero's pack, and while the Sealer stands that pack stays shut: no flask, no bandage, no scroll, nothing that hero walked in with. It takes nothing and breaks nothing - the gear is still in there and it is simply not yours until the press is broken. The strip of lead blanks on its hip is the gauge: one blank is one more pack it can shut, so the party can count the fight it has left before the first bite
sealer.feed_line: Someone down there is stamping lead.

hooper.title: Hoopfast
hooper.idea: IT CASKS ONE OF YOU - it raises a cask over one hero and drives the hoops home, and that hero is not out of the fight: they keep swinging, blind, from inside. What they lose is the party. No heal reaches them, no brew, no shout, no shield - the line can see them and cannot touch them. So the party is not choosing how to kill it, it is choosing whether to spend its swings on the staves to get one of its own back or on the Hooper while one of them fights alone in the dark. The hoops stacked on the post on its back are the gauge: one hoop is one more of you it can shut in, and you can count them the moment it turns
hooper.feed_line: A hoop has just gone on.

relief.title: Watchturn
relief.idea: IT TAKES YOUR POST - it does not hurt anyone and it does not take anyone away. It heaves the gate capstan a quarter turn and THE WHOLE LINE COMES ROUND ONE PLACE: your front rank is at the back, your back rank is at the front, and every reach, guard and heal the party had lined up is now pointing at the wrong body. Nobody is wounded and nobody is missing, so there is nothing to heal and nothing to free - the only answer is to jam the dog in the ratchet plate at its foot, which means spending the fight on a floor plate instead of on the thing hitting you. The FOUR NOTCHES in that plate are the gauge: one notch is one more turn it can take, and the dog sitting in one of them tells you how far round the next is
relief.feed_line: Someone has come to relieve the watch.

scraper.title: Scourstone
scraper.idea: IT RUBS OUT WHAT YOU HAVE JUST DONE - it does not block a blow, it does not heal and it takes nobody away. It works, and when the round is over it draws the stone down the slab and THE LAST THING THE PARTY DID IS UNDONE: the blow that landed comes off, the wound that was closed opens again, the guard that was set is gone. Nothing is kept until something else has been done after it, so the party must get its real work in early and spend its last action on something it is willing to lose. Out-damaging it does not work, because the damage is the thing it takes away - the answer is the STONE PLINTH the slab stands on, and the FIVE CUTS on each of its four faces are the gauge: one cut is one more wipe it has in it, and you can count them from any side of the room
scraper.feed_line: Someone is rubbing a name off the wall.

ferryman.title: Slackwater
ferryman.idea: IT TAKES ONE AT A TIME - the punt holds one, so it has one of you aboard and NOBODY ELSE'S BLOWS LAND. It does not wound, it does not heal and it takes nobody out of the room: it simply will not answer three heroes at once. Whoever it has taken is the only one it can be hurt by, and it chooses - so a party that has stacked its damage on one hero watches that hero stand on the bank while the healer swings a stick at it. The rest are not idle, they are just not fighting IT: they must shift the fare, which is the PEGS ALONG BOTH GUNWALES - one peg is one more crossing it will make, and when the last peg is drawn it has to put the one it holds down and take the next, which is the window. You can count the pegs from any side of the room
ferryman.feed_line: A flat-bottomed boat is being poled up the passage.

winder.title: Haulback
winder.idea: IT WINDS YOU BACK - it has three hooked ropes out across the floor and it does not wound anybody: it takes GROUND. Every turn of the drum drags whoever is hooked back toward the mouth of the chamber, so the party spends a beat buying a yard and the next beat watching it go. Nothing you did is undone and nobody is taken out of the room - you are simply not where you were, and the melee that was about to land is out of reach again. THE COUNT IS THE THREE ROPES, lying on the floor in front of it where anyone can see them: one rope is one hero it can have on at a time, and a rope that is cut stays cut. Cut all three and the drum turns on nothing. The PAWL is why you cannot simply out-pull it - it drops into the ratchet every tooth and the drum does not give a single turn back
winder.feed_line: Something is taking a turn on a drum up ahead.

pitman.title: Underfoot
pitman.idea: IT TAKES THE FLOOR - it does not wound and it does not grab. It digs. Every beat it opens a pit under whoever is standing on the spot it wants, and that delver spends their next beat climbing out on the ladder it leaves them. THE PIT STAYS. It is still there when the fight moves on, so the room the party started in is not the room they finish in: the lines they were holding get cut by holes, and the ground they gave up cannot be taken back. THE COUNT IS THE PIT AT ITS FEET - one mouth, boarded, with a ladder standing out of it, and the spoil it came out of heaped behind.
pitman.feed_line: Someone is digging up ahead, and not for ore.

tither.title: Tenthpart
tither.idea: IT WILL BE PAID - it does not come to kill you and it cannot be driven off. It steps into the way with its balance up and one hand out flat, and it asks for the tenth of what this floor has paid you so far. PAY IT and it stands aside that same beat: no blows, no losses, the set piece is simply OVER and the floor opens. REFUSE IT and the hand closes and it is the hardest thing on this floor, and whatever it puts down it takes the whole purse off. THIS IS THE ONE FIGHT IN HERE THAT NOBODY HAS TO WIN. Every other body in this file is ended by killing it; this one has a second door, and the party chooses which. THE COUNT IS THE PANS - his weight is already in the low one and the one tipped toward you is EMPTY, so a viewer can see what is being asked and that it has not been paid.
tither.feed_line: Something ahead is holding a balance up.

blower.title: Deadair
blower.idea: IT TAKES THE AIR - it does not wound anybody and it does not take anyone away. It works the bellows BACKWARDS and draws the room empty a stroke at a time, and with the air goes what the party does with it: every delver in here acts slower on each stroke, and whoever is carrying the most gives out first. Nothing done to the man slows the count. THE COUNT IS THE BAG - it rides high on his back, pale and ribbed, and it stands one band fuller every stroke, so a viewer can see how long this room has left without being told a number. HOLE THE BAG AND THE COUNT STOPS - and the bag says where to put it: three iron patches are stitched over the places it has been holed before. THIS IS THE ONLY FIGHT IN THIS FILE RUN BY A CLOCK, and the clock is hung on the creature where the party can reach it.
blower.feed_line: Something ahead is drawing the air in.

changer.title: Evenhand
changer.idea: IT TRADES PLACES - whoever hits it hardest ends up standing where it stood. It does not drag anybody to it and it does not take anybody away: it works its post and the two of you come out the other side of each other. Your front rank is now at the back and the thing is standing beside whoever you were keeping out of reach, so the fight punishes the party for landing its best blow and the answer is to choose WHO lands it. THE COUNT IS THE DRUM on top of the post - pale, with three dark rungs, and it turns a third of a turn on every trade, so a viewer can see how many times the room has been shuffled without being told a number. *** THE COUNTERPLAY IS OPEN AND MUST NOT BE READ AS SHIPPED. *** Until 21 Nov this line ended JAM THE ARMS AND IT CANNOT TRADE, and the three bars at hip height were the object that did it. MR. E RULED THEM DELETED AT 22:38 CT and the art lane did not invent a replacement in the same pass. So this creature currently has NO in-world thing a party can stand against to stop the swap, and whoever balances the fight must either accept an unstoppable trade on a cooldown or say what the new answer is. The art lane will build whatever object is named.
changer.feed_line: A turnstile is being worked up ahead.

stopper.title: Chokewell
stopper.idea: IT TAKES THE AIR - the lid comes down a notch at a time and when the last peg drops the room is shut. THIS IS THE ONLY MINIBOSS IN THE SET WITH A DEADLINE: it does not chase you, it does not bar the door and it takes nothing off your back - it stands in the middle of its own ring and screws the lid down, and every notch costs the party wind. Nothing you do to the room buys time back. The one thing that does is getting a shoulder under the ring and lifting, which means standing inside its reach with the hands you wanted for hitting it. THE COUNT IS THE PEGS on the rim - five pale uprights left, one drops every notch - so a viewer can see how long the party has without being told a number, and can see it from the side of the screen where the ring is edge-on. A party that fights this one like the other forty-seven loses to the clock while it is winning on damage.
stopper.feed_line: The air has gone thick. Something is seating a lid.

roper.title: Drawtight
roper.idea: IT TWISTS YOU TOGETHER - it does not wound, it takes nobody away and it does not touch the room. It works its walk backing off from you and takes up slack, and every notch draws the party's shape in: whoever is hindmost is hauled a yard toward the middle. When the last of you is inside one span it lays the rope, and from then on the party stands in ONE PLACE - one footprint, so every sweep in the chamber lands on all of you at once and the formation you were fighting in is gone. THE THING TO READ IS THE TOP IT CARRIES: three strands go into it off the floor and ONE rope comes out the back, which is the whole fight in one object. Nothing you do to it adds slack. The only thing that does is a hero walking OUT, away from the others - which is the one move a party under pressure never wants to make.
roper.feed_line: Something ahead is taking up slack.

almoner.title: Dolehand
almoner.idea: IT DEALS YOUR KIT OUT AGAIN - it does not wound anybody, it takes nothing out of the room and it does not touch the floor. It holds the dole dish out and every delver puts in, and then it gives back - to the wrong hand. While it stands, each hero swings on ANOTHER hero's weapon dice: the knight is working a healer's staff, the rogue is hauling a greatsword it cannot lift. The party's total is UNCHANGED, which is the whole point - nothing is weaker, everything is in the wrong place, and the order you drilled is useless until the dish goes down. THE THING TO READ IS THE PAIR IT CARRIES: a dish held out with three pieces of kit lying in it, and a sack at its hip with two more already dealt back out of the mouth. In and out, on one body.
almoner.feed_line: Something ahead is holding a dish out.

panner.title: Onceround
panner.idea: IT IS SHUT UNTIL THE PAN COMES ROUND - it is not armoured and it is not immune: for most of the fight there is simply NOTHING OF IT TO HIT. The whole creature is a closed drum on a crank, and the one opening in it swings past you once a turn. Blows landed on the shut wall do nothing at all - not reduced, nothing - and the party's problem is no longer how to deal damage but how to HOLD it: everyone who swings early is out of position when the mouth is actually there, and the window is wide enough for a party that waits together and too narrow for one that does not. It does not need to hurt anybody to win; it only has to be shut when you are ready. THE THING TO READ IS THE MOUTH: a shallow wide pan with one open face, lined pale so the hole reads as an opening, canted part-way round so you can see it is TURNING and not parked - and a crank with a handle on the far side that says a thing is driving it.
panner.feed_line: Something ahead is turning, and it is shut.

stiltman.title: Downfast
stiltman.idea: IT IS ALREADY DOWN ONE AND IT IS QUICKER FOR IT - it crosses the room on stilts, it has already lost one, and the pole it feels the bottom with is the only thing holding that end up. The stilt that is left is breakable in plain sight, which is the trap: breaking it WORKS. It comes down, its reach over your front line is gone, and it is FASTER - a shorter stride is a quicker one, and a thing at your own height does not have to stoop to get at you, and it has nothing left to break. Leave it alone and it stands above the party and strikes down past the line into whoever is behind it. It does not choose and it does not time anything: THE PARTY OWNS THE DECISION and both ways cost. THE THING TO READ IS THE LEGS: two bound cuffs at the ankle, ONE POLE ON THE FLOOR and ONE SPLINTERED STUMP hanging clear of it, and a man braced on a crutch where his leg should be.
stiltman.feed_line: Something ahead is walking on poles, and one is gone.

nightman.title: Nightwork
nightman.idea: IT WORKS IN THE DARK AND WAITS IN THE LIGHT - its own shuttered lamp hangs on its belt and the party can work the shutter. OPEN, it stands dead still: it strikes nobody and IT CANNOT BE HURT - a lit nightman is just a man standing in a room, and you can walk past him, and he will still be there when you come back. SHUT, it can be killed - and it WORKS, and a thing that works in the dark is never where you last struck it. So the party owns the switch and both ways cost: hold the lamp open and nothing of it can be finished, shut it and you are fighting something you cannot keep hold of. It does not choose, it does not time anything and it has no phase. THE THING TO READ IS THE LAMP: it is the only bright object on the whole body, it hangs on his own belt where a hand can reach it, and the shutter leaf is standing open beside it.
nightman.feed_line: Someone is working down there, and he brought a lamp.

iceman.title: Hoarback
iceman.idea: IT CARRIES THE COLD AND THE COLD IS ON A COUNT - cut blocks stacked up a back frame, and you can count them from across the room. While a block stands the room is cold and everything in it works slow, HIM INCLUDED: he is not fighting you, he is carrying. The blocks go one at a time in their own time and NOTHING THE PARTY DOES TAKES ONE OFF - you cannot break them, you cannot hurry them, you cannot stop them. When the last one goes the room thaws, and the man who was carrying sets the tongs down and turns round. So the fight is a clock you can SEE and cannot touch: every round of cold is a round you were GIVEN, and the party either spends it - ground, the rest of the room, position, the wounded - or is standing in front of him with nothing done when it runs out. It does not choose and it has no phase; the count is in the geometry. THE THING TO READ IS THE STACK: four pale blocks staggered up a dark frame over a dark man, and a fifth hanging in the tongs.
iceman.feed_line: The walls are sweating, and it is getting colder.

straker.title: Everyhand
straker.idea: IT WILL NOT GO DOWN TO ONE HAND - it is straking a rim, and it will not be finished by anybody who has not put a blow into it. Hurt it all you like with your best hand and it cannot be ended; it keeps a ledger of WHICH OF YOU has struck it, the ledger only grows, and until every hand in the party is on it the last blow does nothing at all. So the party's whole habit is the thing that fails here: the hero who carries every fight cannot carry this one, and the hero the party has spent the floor keeping out of reach has to be walked up to it and made to swing. It does not choose, it has no phase and there is nothing to out-manoeuvre - the condition is on the party, not on the room. THE THING TO READ IS THE RIM: four bright iron strakes laid on the tread of a wheel stood on the floor beside him, one for every hand it is still waiting on, and a hammer held down over the next one.
straker.feed_line: Someone is nailing a rim, and it is not finished.

dredger.title: Finepass
dredger.idea: IT ONLY FEELS WHAT GETS THROUGH THE MESH - it works a dredging sieve in front of it and that sieve IS the creature's whole contact with the room. A heavy blow stops dead on the bars: the harder it is swung the more certainly it is caught and spent, which is the one thing a party never tries, because every instinct says hit it harder. Only a LIGHT hand passes the mesh, so the weakest hand in the file is the only hand that scores, and the hero everybody normally protects is the hero who has to do the killing while the rest of the party keeps the room off them. It does not choose a target, it has no phase, nothing summons and nothing splits - the condition is on HOW HARD YOU SWING, which no other body in this file asks about. THE THING TO READ IS THE SIEVE: one big pale disc held low in both hands, barred across both ways in black, and the bars are plainly what a blow would land on.
dredger.feed_line: Something ahead is dusting the floor.

harrowman.title: Overturn
harrowman.idea: IT IS NOT FIGHTING YOU AND IT WILL NOT TURN ASIDE - it drags a spiked harrow on a fixed round of the room and it works that round whatever is standing on it. It picks nobody, it cannot be interrupted, it has no phase and it does not speed up: a hero caught on the round is taken ALONG with the harrow to the end of the pass and let go there, out of the file and out of position, and the party that was lined up is now strung across the room in the order the harrow dropped them. So the fight is not a target at all, it is GROUND: the round is a moving line you can see coming and the party either keeps off it and fights in the time between passes, or stands its ground and is re-arranged every pass. Hitting it harder does nothing to the round. THE THING TO READ IS THE HARROW: a dark barred lattice dragged low and raked behind him, with bright tines standing down out of it into the floor, and the two traces running from its front corners up over his shoulders to his hands - so a viewer can see that he is HAULING and can see exactly what is being hauled.
harrowman.feed_line: Something is being dragged across the floor up ahead.

pledgeman.title: Heldfast
pledgeman.idea: IT HAS SOMETHING OF YOURS THAT IS NOT YOURS TO SPEND - it has already taken a pledge against the town's debt and it carries that pledge lashed to a board on its back, strapped through its own harness, ALIVE. The pledge takes a share of every blow that lands on the pledgeman, because the two are tied into one load: so the party that fights this the way it fights everything else kills the pledge on the way to the kill, and the room pays out nothing. Nothing is taken from you here and nobody is chosen - the payout is whole when you walk in and the PARTY IS THE ONLY THING IN THE ROOM THAT CAN DESTROY IT. The answer is the three lashings: cut them and the board comes off its back, the pledge drops clear, and what is left is an ordinary heavy brawl with nothing riding on it. So damage is a BUDGET and not a goal, winning the fight and winning the room are two different things, and for the first time in this file hitting it is the wrong move. THE THING TO READ IS THAT THERE ARE TWO BODIES: a stooped man under a raked board slung high off his shoulders, a bound hooded figure lying lashed along that board with its head clear at the top and its feet bound at the bottom, THREE BRIGHT LASHINGS crossing it - the only pale on the whole body, because they are what you are meant to hit - and a strap from each lower corner of the board running over a shoulder into a fist, so a viewer can see that the load is carried and cannot be put down.
pledgeman.feed_line: Someone is being carried who is not walking.

weigher.title: Trueweight
weigher.idea: IT MUST COME DOWN EVEN - it carries a weigh-beam across its shoulders with a pan hanging off either end, and the beam is already tipped. Whatever you put into it goes into the pan on the side you are standing on, and while the beam is tipped the risen side is armoured: the hurt you put into the heavy pan is paid straight back out of the light one. So a party that does what it always does - everybody on one flank, everything into one target - moves this fight nowhere at all, however hard it hits. It has to be brought down LEVEL: both flanks worked at once, both pans loaded together, and the last blow only counts while the beam is even. It does not choose a target, it has no phase and there is nothing to interrupt - the condition is on where the party STANDS. THE THING TO READ IS THE BEAM: two bright pans, one up by his shoulder and one down by his knee, hung off a black bar that is plainly out of true.
weigher.feed_line: A beam is out of true, and something is under it.

crimp.title: Oneshort
crimp.idea: IT TAKES ONE OF YOU INTO ITS OWN CREW - it does not wound, it SIGNS. The hook takes a hero by the collar, the name goes on the muster board, and from that moment that hero is fighting FOR the crimp: the party's own best weapon is in the room swinging at them, at full strength, and it cannot be talked down. Nobody is removed and nothing is stolen, which is what makes this worse than the hook trades - the party is not one short, it is two apart, and killing the signed hero ends the problem the one way the party can never accept. The answer is on the CRIMP and not on the hero: one peg on the board is lit, that peg is the signature, and striking the peg off strikes the name off. So the fight has a target that is not a body, the party has to fight defensively against its own man while someone gets to the board, and the board is deliberately carried out on his off side in clear air where it can be reached - the mechanic is only fair if a viewer can SEE where the answer is kept.
crimp.feed_line: Someone is signing a name in the dark.

timberman.title: Deadfall
timberman.idea: ITS DEATH IS THE DANGER - it is the one prop under a cracked roof. Put it down before its three spares are set and the gallery comes down on the whole room
timberman.feed_line: Something in here is holding the roof up.

collier.title: Halfblow
collier.idea: YOUR OWN HEAVY BLOW IS WHAT OPENS IT - it is earthed shut on a live fire and every blow lands in full, but anything past a measured stroke bursts a vent and the flare takes the whole room. Take it down in half blows, or drive its four pale plugs into the vents first
collier.feed_line: Something in here is shut on a fire.

overlooker.title: Velrick
overlooker.idea: IT STRIKES WHOEVER HAS DONE IT LEAST HARM - it does not pick a hero and it is not dealt a target: it goes for the one who has hurt it least, and it re-reads that the moment it changes. So the back of the room stops being the safe place. A healer who only heals, an archer who holds a shot, anyone who steps out to drink a flask - each of them becomes the target BY DOING THAT, and the hero who has been carrying the fight is the one it will not touch. Hitting it harder does not protect you; it only moves the mark onto whoever did not. The party cannot hold a line against it, because the line is what makes a back rank, and it answers a back rank by walking past the front one. THE THING TO READ IS THE HEAD: it is turned hard off his own shoulders and his cold eyes are on that line, with the pale mitt of his far arm held out level along it - so a viewer can see WHO he has picked before he moves, and can see the pick change.
overlooker.feed_line: Someone up ahead is being watched, and it is not the man in front.

fanner.title: Blastmere
fanner.idea: IT BURNS AS HARD AS YOU CROWD IT - it carries its own hearth on its chest and every delver inside its reach is one more draught on it. One hero alone fights a low red and takes all day about it; the whole line on it at once fights a white heat that answers every one of them. It does not choose a target, it has no phase, nothing summons and nothing splits - the condition is on HOW MANY OF YOU ARE ON IT, which no other body in this file asks about, and it is the one number a party never thinks of as a cost. So the habit that fails here is the first habit a party has: everybody in. THE COUNT IS THE FOUR VANES standing out of the basket rim - one vane is one draught it can still take, they are the only pale on the whole body, and a vane that is broken off stays broken. So the party has two honest answers and both cost: send one hand in and win slowly with the rest of the line standing idle, or spend the early fight breaking vanes off the rim while it is at its hottest and crowd it once they are gone.
fanner.feed_line: Something ahead is being fanned, and it is not a forge.

mealman.title: Whitedamp
mealman.idea: IT MAKES YOUR OWN FIRE THE ROOM'S - it has been working meal in here long enough that the air carries it, and meal in the air is not smoke, it is fuel. While it stands, every point of burning anybody deals lands on EVERY body in this room, its own included, and it does not care who swung. Nothing escalates, nothing is on a count and nothing is summoned: the air is already thick at the doorway and it stays thick until the man stops pouring. So the party's own kit is the trap, and the choice is honest both ways - bench the fire hand and lose that damage for the whole fight, or set the air off on purpose and take the burn yourselves to put a hole in it faster than any blade will. It is the only body in this file you can kill quickest by hurting your own line. WHAT A VIEWER READS IS THE FALL: the pale rope of meal running out of the chute at his shoulder into the trough in his hands, and the drift coming off the trough lip. While that is pouring the air is fuel.
mealman.feed_line: Something ahead is pouring, and the air tastes of flour.

thatcher.title: Lastcourse
thatcher.idea: IT COVERS THE REST - it has been over every other thing in this room with reed before you got here, and while it stands nothing else in here can be hurt at all. Your blows land in thatch. Nothing is summoned, nothing is on a count and it does nothing whatever to itself: it is the only body in this file whose whole effect lands on the OTHER monsters. So the room keeps hitting you at full weight while you cannot hit the room back, and the fight is one question - can you get through what is beating on you to the one man at the back who is not. Kill the thatcher and the covering comes off everything at once. WHAT A VIEWER READS IS THE YEALM: the fat pale bundle of combed reed over his shoulder, banded with three ties and cut square at the butt, and the leggett down in his off hand that he beats it home with. While that is on his shoulder there is more covering where that came from.
thatcher.feed_line: Something ahead has been over this room with reed.
